Here we observe a human... attempting to do one thing.
The brain does not forget things. It reminds you of them. Constantly. At the worst possible moment.
Like a smoke alarm... with a to-do list.
You've tried systems. Four to-do apps. An email to yourself called 'exclamation mark, exclamation mark.' And a sticky note that just says... important.
So this time, you press one key... and say it.
Tucky writes it down. Puts it in the right project. And the loop... stops.
Tasks. Notes. Half-baked ideas. You don't pick a folder. You don't open an app. You just say it, and it lands where it belongs.
You're not remembering to remember anymore. Tucky's got it.
Every morning, Tucky asks one question. What would make today a good day? You answer out loud. A couple of things per project. That's it.
And then it stays. Right there, on your screen.
So when your brain wanders off to research the history of the spoon at two in the afternoon... and it will...
there's your list. Not judging. Much.
Your brain will still do this.
But now it has somewhere to put it.
Tucky. Say it once... then forget it on purpose.
